title: Intervals
summary: The distance between two notes, by name and by ear.

lessons.title: Naming intervals
lessons.summary: Count the letter names, then count the half steps.

blocks.text: An interval is the distance from one note to another. Its number comes from counting letter names, including both ends: C up to E is C, D, E, so it is a third. C up to G is a fifth.

The number alone is not enough, because thirds come in two sizes. Count half steps to find the quality. A major third is four half steps; a minor third is three. A perfect fifth is seven half steps; a perfect fourth is five.
C to E is a major third. C to G is a perfect fifth.

exercise.prompt: What is the interval from C up to E?
exercise.explanation: Three letter names (C, D, E) and four half steps: a major third.

exercise.prompt: How many half steps are in a perfect fifth?
exercise.explanation: Seven half steps, for example C up to G.

blocks.text: Now play the note the app asks for.

lessons.title: Hearing intervals
lessons.summary: Tell a third from a fifth by sound.

blocks.text: Each interval has its own sound. A major third sounds bright and settled, like the start of a major chord. A minor third sounds darker. A perfect fifth sounds open and hollow. An octave sounds like the same note, higher.
The app plays two notes, one after the other and then together. Choose the interval you hear. You can listen as many times as you like.
When you can tell these four apart reliably, the next step is to add the perfect fourth and the major second.
